title: TPK store state
description: state.json in $APPLOCALDATA/tpk/. Each of the three states names the layers it consists of by content hash; promotion is a single atomic write of this file, never a sequence of renames. Layers live in layers/<file_sha256>.tpk and are garbage-collected by reference counting.

pointer.description: Which revision the running process loaded.

install_id.description: Random UUIDv4 generated on first launch. Used for staged-rollout bucketing; survives reset so a device does not re-roll its bucket.

boot_attempts.description: How many times the current booting revision has started without being acknowledged. Below the threshold the revision is retried rather than rolled back: an OS kill, a power loss or a user quitting the app are ordinary events on mobile and must not be mistaken for a bad pack. Cleared by notify_ready.

consecutive_rollbacks.description: At the threshold the client disables auto-check and auto-download and reports degraded status. Blacklisting only breaks the loop for one pack; this breaks it for the device.

last_watermark.description: Highest watermark seen, keyed by channel. A single scalar would make a stable->beta->stable switch discard every stable manifest forever.

min_key_epoch.description: Monotonic floor on signing key generation. Mirrored in keys-cache.json for audit.

file_sha256.description: Also the file name in layers/. Verified once when staged, then tracked by (size, mtime, inode): re-hashing every layer at boot is O(bytes) and blows the startup budget.
